title: The Faithful Letter
premise: In the winter of 1917, at a remote field hospital on a river's far bank, nurse Noor Nakamura secretly records the deaths and deeds that officers leave out of their dispatches. When seasonal floods close the bridge, Noor is trapped with a garrison determined to rewrite its failures as glory — and with a dying colonel who begs them to publish what really happened at the crossing. As the victors' historians arrive by sledge to collect an official account, Noor must choose between safety in silence and smuggling the true ledger across the ice, knowing exposure could cost them everything, including the found family of orderlies and wounded men who have become their only home. The book ends with Noor surrendering the ledger to a young historian who chooses truth over career, allowing the names to survive even as Noor's own role is erased from the record.
about_author: Rosalind Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsent letters from the First World War. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the routine of a snowbound field hospital, Noor tends wounds by day and records unrecorded deaths by night — names the officers' reports omit. The emotional beat is quiet defiance: history happens elsewhere, Noor believes, and this small ledger is a private act, not a mission.

chapters.title: The Colonel Who Counts Wrong
chapters.summary: Colonel Ashworth, dying slowly of a wound no one will treat honestly, notices discrepancies between his own memory of the autumn crossing and the official dispatches. He and Noor circle each other warily; he suspects someone is keeping accounts. Beat: uneasy recognition between two keepers of secrets.

chapters.title: Bridge Closed Until Spring
chapters.summary: The flood season closes the bridge; supply sledges stop, letters stop, and the hospital becomes an island. Noor realizes every escape route now runs through the officers who would burn the ledger if they knew it existed. Beat: claustrophobia — invisibility was a choice until it wasn't.

chapters.title: What Happened at the Crossing
chapters.summary: Ashworth's POV. Feverish, he confesses the truth of the autumn crossing: a retreat ordered too late, three hundred men written off as deserters who died holding the ford. He asks Noor to get it on record before the historians arrive. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Family We Improvised
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor weighs the risk against the household — orderly Tomas, shell-shocked Private Ellery, cook Marta — who have become family without anyone naming it. When Marta discovers the ledger and adds her brother's name to it, secrecy becomes shared trust. Beat: found family as both shelter and stake.

chapters.title: Sledge Tracks on the River Road
chapters.summary: Word arrives: the victors' historians are coming within the fortnight to compile the official account, and Major Renwick — ambitious, frightened of blame — begins coaching witnesses. Noor watches testimony being rehearsed into fiction. Beat: rising dread as the machinery of erasure arrives early.

chapters.title: Renwick's Version
chapters.summary: Major Renwick's POV. Renwick confronts Noor, half-suspecting, offering protection in exchange for loyalty; he reveals the crossing will be recorded as a heroic stand, the dead as volunteers. Noor lies to his face for the first time. Beat: the price of survival made explicit — his survival, bought with theirs.

chapters.title: Ashworth's Last Signature
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Ashworth dies before he can sign a sworn statement; Renwick seals his effects, including a letter corroborating the crossing. Noor steals the letter during the funeral, with Marta and Tomas covering the theft. Beat: climax of commitment — the family now complicit together.

chapters.title: Across the Ice
chapters.summary: With the historians due at dawn, Noor crosses the frozen river at night to reach a telegraph post, pursued by Renwick's patrol. The ice cracks; Noor nearly loses the ledger but saves it, arriving half-frozen to dictate the names and the truth of the crossing to a skeptical young historian, Wren. Beat: climax — the record leaves Noor's hands.

chapters.title: Names That Outlast Us
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, then Noor's. Wren publishes the account, crediting 'an unnamed nurse of the river hospital,' protecting Noor by omission. Back at the hospital, spring opens the bridge, and the family packs to disperse — but Marta's brother's name, and all the others, are now permanent. Beat: bittersweet resolution; identity surrendered so truth survives.
